entities.summary:
The Battle of Emesa was a pivotal event in the history of the Roman Empire, marking a significant turning point in the Roman-Palmyrene Wars. 

It took place in 272 CE, in the city of Homs, Syria, where the Roman Emperor Aurelian clashed with the Palmyrene Queen Zenobia.

The battle resulted in the defeat of the Palmyrene forces, with many of their leaders being captured or killed. Zenobia herself was taken captive and later paraded in Aurelian's triumphal procession in Rome.

The legacy of the Battle of Emesa was far-reaching, as it marked the beginning of the end of Palmyrene independence and the eventual absorption of Palmyra into the Roman Empire. The battle also had significant consequences for the Roman Empire, as it paved the way for Aurelian's subsequent campaigns against the Persians and the consolidation of Roman power in the region.

As the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus noted, 'The fall of Palmyra was a blow from which the East would never recover.'
